column4: Primary landing page; first impression for visitors. Goals: Introduce personal brand, showcase top 3-6 featured projects, display 3 latest blog posts, provide clear navigation to all sections. Target: Recruiters, clients, fellow developers. Metrics: Time on page, click-through rate to projects/blog, bounce rate.

Hero section with name, tagline, and CTA | Featured projects carousel/grid with hover effects | Latest blog posts preview cards | Skills/tech stack visual cloud | Social media links | Download resume button | Animated scroll indicator | Dark/light mode toggle | Newsletter signup (optional)

Components: HeroSection, FeaturedProjects, LatestPosts, SkillsCloud, CTAButton, SocialLinks, Footer. Rendering: SSR for dynamic content (latest posts), static content for hero. State: React Query for server data, Zustand for UI state (theme). Fetching: Parallel API calls for projects + posts using Promise.all. API: GET /api/featured-projects, GET /api/latest-posts. Styling: Tailwind with responsive breakpoints (sm/md/lg/xl). Animations: Framer Motion for entrance animations. Accessibility: Semantic HTML, ARIA labels, skip navigation link.

Models: Project (title, slug, description, tech_stack[], is_featured, order, github_url, live_url, screenshots[], created_at), Post (title, slug, excerpt, content, featured_image, category, tags[], is_published, published_at, author). Views: FeaturedProjectListView (filter: is_featured=True, order_by=order), LatestPostListView (filter: is_published=True, order_by=-published_at[:3]). Serializers: ProjectSerializer (fields: all, depth: 1 for images), PostSerializer (fields: title, slug, excerpt, featured_image, published_at). Endpoints: GET /api/projects/featured/ (200 OK, 404 if empty), GET /api/posts/latest/ (200 OK). Permissions: AllowAny (public). Caching: Redis cache for 1 hour.

1. Browser requests / > Next.js SSR renders shell > calls GET /api/featured-projects + GET /api/latest-posts in parallel. 2. Django receives requests > checks Redis cache > cache miss queries PostgreSQL. 3. Serializers convert QuerySets to JSON > response returned to Next.js. 4. Next.js hydrates React components with data > renders complete page > sends to browser. 5. User clicks project card > client-side navigation to /projects/[slug] > fetches project detail API. Error: Failed API calls show fallback UI with retry button.

Third-party: Framer Motion (animations), React Icons (social icons), next-themes (dark mode). Performance: next/image for optimized images, lazy load below-fold content, preload critical assets. Security: Content Security Policy headers, sanitize user-generated content. SEO: next/head with dynamic meta tags, Open Graph image generation, JSON-LD structured data.

Personal introduction and professional background. Goals: Build trust and credibility, showcase skills and experience, tell professional story. Target: Recruiters evaluating fit, clients considering hiring. Metrics: Resume download count, time spent reading.

Personal bio / summary paragraph | Professional photo | Skills list with proficiency levels | Work experience timeline | Education section | Certifications and awards | Downloadable resume/CV PDF | Social proof (testimonials, GitHub stats) | Personal interests (optional)

Components: AboutHero, BioSection, SkillsList, ExperienceTimeline, EducationSection, ResumeDownload, StatsWidget. Rendering: SSG (content rarely changes, rebuilt on update). State: Local state for interactive timeline, modal for resume preview. Fetching: GET /api/about at build time. Styling: Timeline component with vertical line, skill bars with percentage fills. Animations: Scroll-triggered reveals for timeline items. Accessibility: Proper heading hierarchy (h1 > h2 > h3), alt text for profile photo.

Models: AboutProfile (bio, profile_photo, resume_file, location, email), Skill (name, proficiency_percent, category, order), Experience (company, role, start_date, end_date, description, is_current), Education (institution, degree, field, start_date, end_date). Views: AboutRetrieveView (single object retrieve), SkillListView (filter by category, order_by=order), ExperienceListView (order_by=-start_date). Serializers: AboutProfileSerializer, SkillSerializer, ExperienceSerializer, EducationSerializer. Endpoints: GET /api/about/ (200 OK), GET /api/skills/ (200 OK), GET /api/experience/ (200 OK). Media: profile_photo and resume_file served via WhiteNoise/S3.

1. Build time: Next.js calls GET /api/about/ during static generation. 2. Django returns profile data with related skills, experience, education (select_related/prefetch_related). 3. Next.js embeds data in static HTML at build time. 4. On page load, static HTML served from CDN > hydration adds interactivity. 5. User clicks timeline item > expands detail via local state (no API call). Resume download: GET /media/resume.pdf served by Nginx/WhiteNoise.

Third-party: react-vertical-timeline-component (timeline UI), react-countup (animated stats). Performance: SSG means instant load; optimize profile photo with next/image. Security: Resume PDF scan for malware, restrict media access. SEO: Rich structured data for Person schema (name, jobTitle, alumniOf, knowsAbout).

Comprehensive portfolio showcase. Goals: Display all projects with filtering/search, enable deep-dive into individual projects, demonstrate technical breadth and depth. Target: Technical hiring managers, potential clients. Metrics: Project detail views, filter usage, external link clicks (GitHub/live demo).

Project grid with thumbnail cards | Category filters (Web, Mobile, API, etc.) | Technology stack filters | Search by title/description | Sort options (recent, featured, alphabetical) | Pagination or infinite scroll | Project detail page with full description | Image gallery/screenshots carousel | Links to GitHub and live demo | Related projects section

Components: ProjectsPage (layout with filters + grid), ProjectCard, ProjectFilters (category, tech, search), ProjectGrid, ProjectDetailPage, ImageGallery, TechBadgeList, RelatedProjects. Rendering: List page SSR/CSR with filters, detail pages ISR (revalidate: 3600). State: URL query params for filter state (shareable), Zustand for UI state. Fetching: GET /api/projects?category=X&tech=Y&search=Z&page=1. Routing: /projects (list), /projects/[slug] (detail). Styling: CSS Grid for responsive layout (1/2/3 columns), hover effects on cards. Accessibility: Filter announcements via aria-live, keyboard navigation for pagination.

Models: Project (title, slug, description, short_description, category, tech_stack[], github_url, live_url, featured_image, screenshots[], is_featured, order, created_at, updated_at), ProjectCategory (name, slug, description). Views: ProjectListView (filtering via django-filter: category, tech_stack__contains, search across title/description; pagination: 12/page), ProjectDetailView (lookup by slug). Serializers: ProjectListSerializer (lightweight: title, slug, short_description, featured_image, category, tech_stack[]), ProjectDetailSerializer (full: all fields + related projects). Endpoints: GET /api/projects/ (200 OK, pagination metadata), GET /api/projects/{slug}/ (200 OK, 404). Filtering: SearchFilter, DjangoFilterBackend. Optimization: select_related for category, prefetch_related for screenshots.

List page: 1. User loads /projects > Next.js renders with initial SSR data (page 1, no filters). 2. User selects filter > URL updates (?category=web) > React Query fetches filtered results. 3. Django processes filters > returns paginated JSON with count, next, previous, results[]. 4. Frontend updates grid with new data. Detail page: 1. User clicks project card > navigates to /projects/[slug]. 2. ISR serves pre-rendered page if exists, otherwise SSR. 3. Related projects fetched via GET /api/projects?exclude=current_slug&category=same&limit=3.

Third-party: yet-another-react-lightbox (image gallery), react-share (social sharing). Performance: Image optimization via next/image with blur placeholder, ISR for fast detail pages, lazy load images below fold. Security: Validate slug format, prevent SQL injection via ORM, rate limit project detail API. SEO: Dynamic meta tags per project, Open Graph images from featured_image, sitemap.xml with all project URLs.

Blog post listing and discovery. Goals: Present articles in an organized, searchable manner, drive readership, establish thought leadership. Target: Developers, tech community, potential employers. Metrics: Page views per post, average read time, subscription rate, social shares.

Post cards with title, excerpt, featured image, author, date | Category sidebar/filter | Tag cloud | Search functionality | Pagination | Sort by date/popularity | Reading time estimate | RSS feed link | Newsletter signup | Author profile cards

Components: BlogPage, PostCard, CategorySidebar, TagCloud, SearchBar, Pagination, SortDropdown, NewsletterForm. Rendering: SSR for SEO (posts list), SSG for category/tag pages. State: URL params for filters/search/sort/page, React Query for server state. Fetching: GET /api/posts?page=1&category=X&tag=Y&search=Z&ordering=-published_at. Routing: /blog (list), /blog/[slug] (detail), /blog/category/[slug], /blog/tag/[slug]. Styling: Clean typography-focused design, card-based layout. Accessibility: Proper article semantics, skip to content link, screen reader announcements for search results.

Models: Post (title, slug, content, excerpt, featured_image, author [FK to User], category [FK], tags [M2M], status [draft/published], published_at, created_at, updated_at, view_count), Category (name, slug, description), Tag (name, slug), Comment (post [FK], author_name, author_email, content, is_approved, created_at). Views: PostListView (filtering: category, tags__slug, search across title/excerpt/content; ordering: -published_at, -view_count; pagination: 10/page), PostDetailView (lookup by slug, increment view_count). Serializers: PostListSerializer (id, title, slug, excerpt, featured_image, author_name, published_at, reading_time, category_name), PostDetailSerializer (all fields + comments[] + related_posts[]). Endpoints: GET /api/posts/ (200 OK), GET /api/posts/{slug}/ (200 OK, 404), GET /api/categories/ (200 OK), GET /api/tags/ (200 OK). Search: Full-text search using PostgreSQL SearchVector on title + content + excerpt.

List: 1. User navigates to /blog > Next.js SSR fetches page 1 posts. 2. User types in search > debounced API call to GET /api/posts?search=query. 3. Django uses PostgreSQL full-text search > returns filtered results. 4. Frontend updates post list without full reload. Detail: 1. User clicks post > navigates to /blog/[slug]. 2. ISR serves pre-rendered page; if stale, revalidates in background. 3. GET /api/posts/{slug}/ returns post with comments. 4. View count incremented atomically (F() expression to avoid race conditions). Comments: POST /api/posts/{slug}/comments/ with name, email, content > moderation queue (is_approved=False by default).

Third-party: react-markdown / MDX for content rendering, react-syntax-highlighter for code blocks, RSS package for feed generation. Performance: ISR with staggered revalidation, image optimization, code splitting for markdown renderer. Security: XSS prevention via markdown sanitization, CSRF protection on comment form, Akismet spam filtering, rate limiting on comments. SEO: Article structured data (headline, author, datePublished), meta description from excerpt, canonical URLs.

Individual article display with rich reading experience. Goals: Deliver content in a clean, readable format, encourage engagement (comments, shares), suggest related content. Target: Readers interested in specific topics. Metrics: Time on page, scroll depth, comment count, social shares.

Rich text / Markdown rendering with syntax highlighting | Author byline with avatar | Publication date and reading time | Category and tags | Social share buttons (Twitter, LinkedIn, copy link) | Prev/next post navigation | Related posts section | Comment form and comment list | Table of contents (auto-generated from headings) | Newsletter CTA at end of post | Post reactions/likes (optional)

Components: PostDetailPage, PostHeader, PostContent (Markdown renderer), TableOfContents, AuthorCard, ShareButtons, PostNavigation, RelatedPosts, CommentSection, CommentForm, CommentList, NewsletterCTA. Rendering: ISR (revalidate: 3600) or SSG for popular posts, fallback: blocking for new posts. State: React Query for post data, local state for TOC active section, comment form state. Fetching: GET /api/posts/{slug}, POST /api/posts/{slug}/comments. Styling: Typography scale for headings (h1-h4), code blocks with dark theme, blockquotes styled distinctly. Accessibility: Article landmark, skip to comments link, focus management after comment submission.

Models: Same as Blog list (Post, Category, Tag, Comment). Views: PostDetailView (retrieve by slug, atomically increment view_count), CommentCreateView (create comment for post, set is_approved=False pending moderation). Serializers: PostDetailSerializer (all Post fields + author details + category + tags[] + comments[approved_only=True] + related_posts[3] + prev/next slugs), CommentSerializer (id, author_name, content, created_at). Endpoints: GET /api/posts/{slug}/ (200 OK, 404 Not Found), POST /api/posts/{slug}/comments/ (201 Created, 400 Validation Error). Related posts: Find posts sharing most tags, exclude current, limit 3. View count: Use F('view_count') + 1 to prevent race conditions. Permission: Comments allow anonymous (name + email required).

1. User navigates to /blog/[slug] > Next.js checks ISR cache. 2. Cache hit: serve static; cache miss: SSR fetch from GET /api/posts/{slug}/. 3. Django retrieves post with select_related('author', 'category') + prefetch_related('tags', 'comments'). 4. Serializer builds response with post + author profile + approved comments + related posts + prev/next navigation. 5. HTML rendered with react-markdown hydrating content. Comments: 1. User fills comment form (name, email, content) > POST to /api/posts/{slug}/comments/. 2. Backend validates > saves with is_approved=False. 3. Returns 201; frontend shows 'comment pending moderation' message. 4. Admin approves via Django admin; comment appears on next page load.

Third-party: react-markdown + remark-gfm (GitHub flavored markdown), rehype-highlight (syntax highlighting), react-share (social buttons), reading-time (estimate). Performance: ISR for instant loads, lazy load comments section, defer non-critical third-party scripts. Security: bleach/sanitize HTML in markdown output, CSRF token on comment form, honeypot field for spam, rate limit: 5 comments per hour per IP. SEO: Article schema markup, canonical URL, meta description from excerpt, Open Graph with featured image.

Enable visitors to send messages and get in touch. Goals: Provide easy communication channel, capture leads/inquiries, display alternative contact methods. Target: Potential clients, recruiters, collaboration seekers. Metrics: Form submission rate, response time, conversion to meetings.

Contact form (name, email, subject, message) | Form validation with error messages | reCAPTCHA v3 integration | Success/error toast notifications | Social media links (GitHub, LinkedIn, Twitter) | Email address display (with copy button) | Location/timezone info | Calendly/booking link integration (optional) | FAQ section (optional)

Components: ContactPage, ContactForm, FormInput, FormTextarea, SocialLinks, ContactInfoCard, SuccessToast, ErrorToast. Rendering: SSG (mostly static). State: Form state with react-hook-form (validation rules), submission status (idle/submitting/success/error). Fetching: POST /api/contact/ with form data + recaptcha token. Validation: Client-side (required fields, email format, min length) + server-side. Styling: Clean form layout with floating labels, focus states. Accessibility: Proper form labeling, error announcement via aria-describedby, focus management on submit.

Models: ContactMessage (name, email, subject, message, recaptcha_token, ip_address, created_at, is_read). Views: ContactCreateView (POST only, handles form submission). Validation: Validate all fields present, email format, message length (10-2000 chars), verify reCAPTCHA token with Google API. Email: On valid submission, send email to site owner via Django send_mail() with message details. Rate limiting: Max 3 submissions per IP per hour using Django Ratelimit or custom middleware. Serializers: ContactSerializer (fields: name, email, subject, message, recaptcha_token; read_only: created_at). Endpoints: POST /api/contact/ (201 Created on success, 400 Validation Error, 429 Rate Limited). Admin: ContactMessage listed in Django admin with is_read status filter.

1. User fills contact form > client-side validation passes. 2. reCAPTCHA v3 executes in background > returns token. 3. Frontend POST {name, email, subject, message, recaptcha_token} to /api/contact/. 4. Backend validates fields > verifies reCAPTCHA with Google (score >= 0.5). 5. If valid: saves ContactMessage to database > sends notification email to ADMIN_EMAIL > returns 201. 6. Frontend shows success toast > resets form. Error flow: Validation fails > 400 with field errors > frontend displays per-field errors. Rate limit exceeded > 429 > show 'try again later' message.

Third-party: Google reCAPTCHA v3 (spam prevention), react-hook-form (form management), react-hot-toast (notifications). Performance: Lightweight page, minimal API calls. Security: reCAPTCHA verification server-side (never trust client), rate limiting by IP, email content sanitization, log spam attempts. Privacy: GDPR-compliant (no data storage without consent checkbox), clear privacy policy link. Email: Configure Django EMAIL_BACKEND (SMTP/ SendGrid/AWS SES), async sending via Celery to avoid blocking response.
